question.prompt: The distance light travels in one year is approximately \(5{,}870{,}000{,}000{,}000\) miles. The distance light travels in \(100\) years is:

solutions.explanation:
Light travels the same distance each year, so the distance in \(100\) years is \(100\) times the one-year distance. Write the given approximation as \(5.87\times10^{12}\) miles. Since \(100=10^2\), multiplying the powers of ten adds their exponents:
\[
100(5.87\times10^{12})=5.87\times10^{14}.
\]
To match the coefficient \(587\) in the choices, multiply \(5.87\) by \(100\) and divide its power-of-ten factor by \(100\):
\[
5.87\times10^{14}=587\times10^{12}.
\]
Thus the distance is approximately \(\boxed{587\times10^{12}\text{ miles}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Multiply the yearly distance by 100
